rows.claim: People expect a cached zero price to be reused, a 0 tax rate to mean no tax, and a price cached exactly 60,000 ms ago to still be fresh, but the code really treats a zero cached price as a miss, replaces a 0 tax rate with 0.2, and treats an entry exactly 60,000 ms old as stale.

People expect a tax rate of 0 to mean no tax, a cached price of 0 to be reused, and a cached price to be reused until 60 seconds have passed, but the code really treats 0 tax as the default 20 percent, treats a cached 0 price as a miss because it checks truthiness, and refetches once the entry is at least 60000 ms old.

People expect run_import to import the same records every time it is called and to report sink failures, but the code really reuses dedupe's mutable default seen set so a second identical import writes nothing, and it silently skips any batch whose sink raises ValueError.

People expect run_import to import the same records again on a second call and to surface a failed batch, but the code really reuses dedupe's mutable default seen set so a second identical call writes nothing and silently skips any batch whose sink raises ValueError.

People expect fetchAllOrders to keep retrying a rate-limited request until it succeeds and to return every order, but the code really throws HTTP 429 after four total 429 responses and silently returns only the first five pages when more pages remain.

People expect fetchAllOrders to fetch every order or fail loudly and to keep retrying a rate-limited request until it succeeds, but the code really silently returns only the first 5 pages of ids and throws HTTP 429 after the fourth consecutive 429 response despite three backoff retries.

People expect report to average the two middle latencies for an even number of successful routes and to give a clear empty result when none succeed, but the code really returns the upper middle latency and returns undefined for slowest, median, and fastest when no route is successful.

People expect report to average the two middle latencies for an even number of successful routes and to give a clear empty result when none succeed, but the code really returns the upper middle latency as the median and returns undefined for slowest, median, and fastest when no route succeeds.

People expect withRetry to throw the original 429 error immediately after the third and final failed attempt, but the code really sleeps for another 400ms backoff after that last failure and then throws a new Error with message 'gave up' instead.

People expect withRetry to give up immediately after the third retryable failure and to retry transient failures generally, but the code really sleeps for another 400ms after that final 429 failure before throwing 'gave up' and it retries only errors whose message contains '429'.
